heroTitle: Three paths across shared historical space-time
heroLead: From mythic and traditional origins through early Chinese thought, Buddhist source regions and later transmission, trace Dao, Ru and Fo through people, events, places, texts and later influence on a living map.

todayPassage.quote: Form is not different from emptiness; emptiness is not different from form.
todayPassage.interpretation: The line does not dismiss reality. It challenges the idea that things possess an isolated and unchanging essence.

exhibition.title: Chang'an: Where the Three Traditions Met
exhibition.subtitle: 长安：三教相遇的世界之都
exhibition.question: Why did one empire draw on Daoist institutions, Confucian ritual order and Buddhist teaching at the same time?

traditions.label: Dao
traditions.subtitle: 道
traditions.statement: Follow texts, mountains, institutions and lineages to distinguish Daoist thought from organised Daoism.

traditions.label: Ru
traditions.subtitle: 儒
traditions.statement: Follow ritual, classical learning and state education to see Confucian traditions embedded in imperial institutions.

traditions.label: Buddhism
traditions.subtitle: 佛
traditions.statement: Follow pilgrimage, translation and monasteries to see how an imported tradition found new forms in China.

featuredFigures.title: Laozi (Li Er)
featuredFigures.role: Source figure · tradition and biography
featuredFigures.summary: A recognisable gateway into Daoist classicism; figure, text attribution and later sacralisation remain distinct layers.
featuredFigures.timeLabel: Late Spring and Autumn period; contested

featuredFigures.title: Sima Chengzhen
featuredFigures.role: Tang Daoist master · mountain and institution
featuredFigures.summary: Connects mountain cultivation, Daoist lineages and Tang imperial patronage.

featuredFigures.title: Confucius (Kong Qiu)
featuredFigures.role: Source figure · speech and transmission
featuredFigures.summary: A gateway into Confucian classics, education and political ethics; Analects layers remain separate.

featuredFigures.title: Kong Yingda
featuredFigures.role: Tang classical scholar · education and commentary
featuredFigures.summary: Represents how Tang classical learning entered state education, commentary and institutional knowledge production.

featuredFigures.title: Śākyamuni Buddha (Gautama)
featuredFigures.role: Source figure · early texts and sacred place
featuredFigures.summary: Connects Buddhist thought, early textual transmission and pilgrimage geography without collapsing history and sacred narrative.

featuredFigures.title: Xuanzang
featuredFigures.role: Pilgrimage and translation · Chang'an network
featuredFigures.summary: Connects a pilgrimage for learning with translation and institutional life in Chang'an.

featuredFigures.title: Cheng Xuanying
featuredFigures.role: Early Tang interpreter · texts and knowledge networks
featuredFigures.summary: An entry into Daodejing and Zhuangzi interpretation and Daoist knowledge networks; life and commentary transmission remain under review.

featuredFigures.title: Jizang
featuredFigures.role: Sui–Tang Buddhist thinker · teaching and commentary
featuredFigures.summary: Uses teaching, writings and institutions to approach Buddhist thought and textual interpretation while retaining historical layers in school labels.

featuredFigures.title: Li Shimin
featuredFigures.role: Tang Taizong · institutions and urban context
featuredFigures.summary: Places courtly, educational and religious institutions in the context of Chang'an as a meeting point for networks of knowledge and belief.

featuredFigures.title: Wu Zhao (Wu Zetian)
featuredFigures.role: Ruler of Zhou · ritual and memory
featuredFigures.summary: Places political power, religious patronage and later memory side by side to show how one figure is written across traditions.

featuredFigures.title: Yan Shigu
featuredFigures.role: Early Tang editor · official learning and commentary
featuredFigures.summary: Connects classical editing and commentary with state knowledge projects; specific offices and projects remain pending item-level review.

featuredFigures.title: Yijing
featuredFigures.role: Pilgrim and translator · maritime networks
featuredFigures.summary: Connects maritime pilgrimage, South Asian learning and Chinese Buddhist translation, adding a route beyond Xuanzang's overland journey.

featuredFigures.title: Zhuangzi (Zhuang Zhou)
featuredFigures.role: Warring States thinker · composite textual tradition
featuredFigures.summary: Connects parabolic philosophy, biography and layered Zhuangzi chapters; a regional map anchor does not replace an exact itinerary.
featuredFigures.timeLabel: c. fourth century BCE; textual layers contested

featuredFigures.title: Mencius (Meng Ke)
featuredFigures.role: Itinerant counsel · human nature and canonisation
featuredFigures.summary: Connects Warring States counsel and political ethics with the transmitted and compiled Mengzi.

featuredFigures.title: Zhang Daoling
featuredFigures.role: Celestial Masters origins · historical and sacred founder layers
featuredFigures.summary: Places Eastern Han clues, Celestial Masters lineages and later sacralisation in distinct relation layers.
featuredFigures.placeLabel: Heming Mountain · tradition and memory space

featuredFigures.title: Ge Hong
featuredFigures.role: Eastern Jin thinker · Baopuzi and cultivation knowledge
featuredFigures.summary: Connects textual work, Daoist knowledge and later Mount Luofu memory while keeping biography and immortality narratives distinct.
featuredFigures.placeLabel: Mount Luofu · regional and memory anchor

featuredFigures.title: Ashoka
featuredFigures.role: Mauryan ruler · edicts and dhamma policy
featuredFigures.summary: Uses inscriptions, governance and Buddhist heritage to trace circulation without equating later biography with edict evidence.
featuredFigures.placeLabel: Sanchi · real site and material memory

featuredFigures.title: Nāgārjuna
featuredFigures.role: Madhyamaka thinker · attribution and reception
featuredFigures.summary: Connects Madhyamaka debate, the Mūlamadhyamakakārikā and later Chinese transmission while keeping dating contested.

featuredFigures.title: Kumarajiva
featuredFigures.role: Translator · Kucha–Chang'an knowledge movement
featuredFigures.summary: Connects transregional movement, Chang'an translation institutions and Chinese Buddhist-text production as collaborative work.

featuredFigures.title: Faxian
featuredFigures.role: Pilgrim and recorder · transregional route
featuredFigures.summary: Connects pilgrimage, monastic observations and the Foguoji, adding a knowledge route beyond Xuanzang.

featuredFigures.title: Pangu
featuredFigures.role: Mythic persona · cosmogenesis
featuredFigures.summary: An entry into creation and cosmic order narratives; it is not mapped to real historical geography.
featuredFigures.timeLabel: Mythic time: no single historical date

featuredFigures.title: Nuwa
featuredFigures.role: Mythic persona · creation and repair
featuredFigures.summary: Connects creation, repair and restored order while later visual and cult memory remains separately marked.
featuredFigures.timeLabel: Mythic time: no single historical date

featuredFigures.title: Fu Xi
featuredFigures.role: Mythic persona · trigrams and order
featuredFigures.summary: Approaches Fu Xi through symbols, classification and cosmic order without claiming a verifiable personal invention history.
featuredFigures.timeLabel: Mythic time: no single historical date

featuredFigures.title: Huangdi (Yellow Emperor)
featuredFigures.role: Legendary figure · ancestry and order
featuredFigures.summary: Places Five Emperors traditions, political symbolism and later state memory together without a false birth date.
featuredFigures.timeLabel: Legendary time: no verifiable birth date

featuredFigures.title: Xi Wangmu (Queen Mother of the West)
featuredFigures.role: Sacred figure · Kunlun and immortality
featuredFigures.summary: Connects Kunlun, immortality and sacred-female imagery while real geography and mythic space remain distinct.
featuredFigures.timeLabel: Mythic and sacred traditional time: no single historical date

featuredFigures.title: Taishang Laojun
featuredFigures.role: Sacred figure · later sacralisation of Laozi
featuredFigures.summary: A distinct identity connected to Laozi through deification and Daoist sacred genealogy in celestial space.

methodologyTitle: History, tradition and myth do not share one label
methodologyText: Key content separates documented evidence, traditional accounts and interpretation; real geography is separated from sacred geography; passages retain a version and locator.
